name: SpaceX
day_summary: Day 4 and the first red session since IPO. SPCX opened at $208.24, extended to a session high of $213.80 (+5.9%) as the MSCI passive bid absorbed early sellers — then the 2:00 PM ET FOMC release and Warsh's 2:30 PM press conference erased the gain and more. The stock plunged to a session low of $187.01 (-7.3% from prior close) before recovering into the close at $191.82 (-4.95%). Volume of 200.5M shares was 38% below the 324.7M session average — the below-average volume on the first real selloff is the one constructive data point: no institutional panic despite a $26.79 intraday reversal from high to low. Two bear voices emerged publicly: veteran short-seller Jim Chanos warned that investors rarely profit from buying stocks valued above 100x revenue with net losses (SPCX is at ~93x revenue), and a former Nasdaq chief stated the rally reflects sentiment and thin-float mechanics, not fundamental value. The hawkish FOMC outcome — 9/18 members projecting 2026 rate hikes, median rate raised to 3.8%, Warsh dropping forward guidance — hit high-multiple growth names hardest; SPCX fell alongside Meta (-5.44%), MSFT (-3.79%), AMZN (-3.46%). Options delta-hedging by market makers mechanically amplified the intraday decline through $200. The critical evening update: Iran's foreign ministry confirmed both Trump and President Pezeshkian digitally signed the ceasefire memorandum as of June 17, with the agreement in immediate effect; the Geneva ceremony originally scheduled June 19 may be superseded by the digital signing. This removes the Iran blocking condition from the SPCX entry framework — the $190–$200 zone is now live per the pre-established conditions.

analysis:
## Day 4: First red session — the FOMC delivers the entry zone

SPCX closed at **$191.82**, down 4.95% from Tuesday's $201.80 — the first decline since the June 13 IPO debut. The day's structure told the whole story of what a 4% float looks like at $2.08T market cap: opened at $208.24, extended to **$213.80** (+5.9%) as the MSCI passive bid absorbed early sellers, then the 2:00 PM ET FOMC release and Warsh's 2:30 PM press conference erased the gain in real time. By the FOMC session lows, SPCX had fallen to **$187.01** — a $26.79 intraday reversal from the high. The close at $191.82 represents partial recovery but the session ended well below any prior daily close.

## Technical analysis

**Trend:** SPCX is in its first pullback from the IPO launch. Four-day high was $225.64; four sessions later the stock is at $191.82 — a -15% drawdown from the ATH. This is a standard post-IPO correction after a float-squeeze move. The trend is still technically up from $135 IPO (+42%), but the Day 4 volume deceleration to 200.5M (vs 324.7M Day 3) is the first momentum divergence.

**Volume — the most constructive signal:** [200.5M shares vs 324.7M average](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-stock-falls-for-first-time-ending-3-day-surge-150808757.html) is **38% below average** on a -4.95% session that included the most hawkish FOMC in four years. When supply can't surge on the best possible macro catalyst for bears, it typically means the institutional long book is sticky. The exact same pattern appeared in NVDA today (-1.33% on 126M vs 157M average). Below-average volume on a down day is a classic bullish divergence signal.

**Pattern:** The intraday structure (high $213.80 → low $187.01 → close $191.82) is a wide-range reversal candle with a partial recovery. For a normally-traded stock, this would be immediately bearish. For SPCX with its MSCI passive bid and 4% float, the question is whether the passive bid returns into Friday (June 20) options expiry. Max pain at $195 provides a natural floor above current price.

**★ Strongest support — $190–$200 entry zone:** This zone was pre-positioned in prior briefs as the defined-risk entry with a put hedge. The FOMC has delivered the pullback. The framework entry is active. The only open question is sequencing within the STEP_ASIDE regime (see below).

**★ Strongest resistance — $200 round number:** SPCX held above $200 for all of Days 1–3. Day 4 closed at $191.82 — the first daily close below $200. $200 is now resistance until reclaimed on a daily close basis with above-average volume.

## Why FOMC hit SPCX harder than NVDA

NVDA fell -1.33%; SPCX fell -4.95%. The difference is valuation sensitivity. NVDA trades at ~30x forward P/E on a $91B revenue run rate with 62-analyst coverage — expensive but DCF-defensible. SPCX at **~93x 2025 revenue** with net losses has no DCF anchor; its entire valuation is multiple expansion. As Warsh raised the 2026 median rate to 3.8% and implied hike risks, the denominator in every SPCX DCF moved up simultaneously. [Options delta-hedging](https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-spacex-stock-sliding-today-93CH-4696238) mechanically amplified the decline: as SPCX fell through $200, market makers short puts delta-hedged by selling SPCX, pushing it to $187.01 before the natural floor of the passive bid absorbed supply.

## The Chanos and Nasdaq-chief warnings: right thesis, uncertain timing

[TradingKey's former Nasdaq chief commentary](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/261972394-spacex-stock-forecast-spcx-falls-from-225-to-206-is-the-rally-running-out-tradingkey) and Jim Chanos's warning (investors rarely profit buying above 100x revenue with net losses) are both structurally correct. But 'correct' and 'timely' diverge when there is a forced buyer. The MSCI passive bid doesn't read Chanos — it buys the index weight. Zephirin Group's Buy with $310 PT (and 5 analysts recommending buy vs 1 sell) is the institutional counter-view. The bet is on sequencing: whether the fundamental repricing happens before or after the passive bid exhausts (est. 2–4 weeks).

## Iran deal: the blocking condition is gone

The most important post-close development: [Iran's foreign ministry confirmed both presidents digitally signed the ceasefire memorandum on June 17](https://www.rappler.com/world/middle-east/us-iran-presidents-sign-ceasefire-deal-june-2026/), with the agreement in immediate effect. The Geneva ceremony originally scheduled for June 19 may be superseded by the digital signing. Per the prior brief's entry framework: 'June 20 Monday open IF Iran signs June 19 AND Brent holds below $82.' Iran signed June 17 — the condition is met (one session earlier). Brent at ~$78 is below $82. Both pre-conditions for re-entry are now satisfied. The only remaining gating factor is the STEP_ASIDE macro regime (VIX 18.44). That regime gate justifies the 50% entry size and mandatory put hedge — not indefinite inaction.
